concept.subject: Dandelion clocks seen from below against a soft blue-gray sky, two big seed heads and three small ones on long green stems.
concept.composition: A big seed head stands left of the middle a little below half height, another right of the cannon at a third of the height on a long stem leaning down to the left; small heads sit low on the left, on the right at mid height and cut by the right edge higher up; the stems rise from low shrubs along the bottom.
concept.layout: 144 round pegs. The big seed heads are two concentric rings with a center peg and a stem of pegs below; the small ones are rings, the right one with a center peg and the one at the edge an arc. Wind ribbons curl into spirals in the open sky, one in the upper left and a larger one between the big heads; curls, seed trails and two low waves of wind between the stems spread the rest, with a single seed under the cannon and a short line up the closed bud on the right.

background.prompt: A photo of dandelion clocks seen from below against a soft blue-gray sky with a few pale clouds. A big seed head is centered at about 29 percent of the width and 56 percent of the height, about a quarter of the picture wide; another, about a fifth of the picture wide, is centered at about 69 percent of the width and 35 percent of the height on a long stem that leans down to the left to about three fifths of the width at the bottom. Small seed heads sit low on the left at about a tenth of the width and seven tenths of the height, on the right at about 89 percent of the width and three fifths of the height, and cut by the right edge at about 28 percent of the height. A closed bud rises at about 86 percent of the width near the bottom, and low shrubs line the bottom edge.

picture.title: Artistic dandelion sculptures reaching up to a clear blue sky in Seoul, capturing the essence of nature and creativity.
picture.author: Andrea De Santis
